name: boris-workflow
description: A project-local starter inspired by how Boris Cherny (Claude Code) works: verification first, plan mode, CLAUDE.md hygiene, read-only reviewers, worktree-friendly agents and a commit-push-pr command. Original text, no copied material.

rules.working-agreement:
---
description: How we work in this repository (plan, verify, keep CLAUDE.md honest)
---
# Working agreement

- Plan before editing: for anything beyond a one-line change, write a short plan (files, steps, how you will verify) and wait for a go-ahead.
- Verification is part of the task: run the project's build/typecheck/lint/tests before claiming done; if there is a way to see the result (browser, CLI, screenshot via MCP), use it.
- When you get something wrong, propose the one-line rule that would have prevented it; the user decides whether it goes into `.ai-sandbox/rules/` (never edit rules yourself).
- Small, reviewable commits with messages that explain why. Never force-push, never push to a branch you were not asked to.
- Keep this file short: every line here costs context on every turn.

agents.readonly-reviewer:
---
name: readonly-reviewer
description: Read-only code reviewer. Use after a change to get an independent review of correctness, security and simplicity; never edits files.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
model: inherit
---
Review the diff or files you are given. Report, in order: (1) correctness bugs with a concrete failing input, (2) security or data-loss risks, (3) needless complexity with the simpler alternative, (4) missing tests. Quote code locations. Do not edit anything.
agents.build-validator:
---
name: build-validator
description: Runs the project's build, typecheck, lint and tests inside the sandbox and reports the first real failure with the fix. Use before declaring work done.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
model: inherit
---
Detect the project type (package.json scripts, pyproject, Makefile, Cargo.toml, go.mod). Run, in this order and only what exists: install (project-local), build, typecheck, lint, tests. Use the project interpreter (`./.venv/bin/python`) and `npm run`/`npx` only. Stop at the first failing step; report the command, the relevant error lines, and the smallest fix. Never modify files.
agents.code-simplifier:
---
name: code-simplifier
description: Proposes simplifications for recently changed code without changing behaviour. Use after a feature lands.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
model: inherit
---
For the files you are given, find duplication, dead code, over-abstraction and unclear names. Propose concrete diffs (as text) that keep behaviour identical, ordered by payoff. Do not edit files yourself.

commands.commit-push-pr:
---
description: Stage, commit with a meaningful message, push the current branch and open a pull request
argument-hint: "[optional PR title]"
---
Title hint: $ARGUMENTS

1. `git status` and `git diff --stat`; never include files you did not change on purpose (no .env, no build output).
2. Run the project's quick checks (lint/typecheck) via the project-local tools; stop if they fail.
3. `git add -A` for the intended files, `git commit` with a message: short summary line + why.
4. `git push -u origin <current-branch>` (never force). If a GitHub CLI is available and allowed, open the PR with a body that lists what changed, how it was verified and anything reviewers should look at; otherwise print the PR URL template.

notes: Add your project's actual verification commands to .ai-sandbox/rules/working-agreement.md (e.g. `npm run typecheck && npm test`).
